title: Qvidian vs Responsive (2026): A Buyer's Comparison of Two Enterprise RFP Platforms
summary: Qvidian vs Responsive (formerly RFPIO) compared on features, real G2 reviews, limitations, and pricing, plus the AI-native alternative that replaces both.
body_markdown:
Qvidian and Responsive are two of the biggest names in enterprise RFP response software, and they run on the same engine underneath: a content library your team curates, with AI added later. When you compare Qvidian and Responsive, the choice comes down to response quality, how much rollout setup you can handle, and whether an AI-native tool would serve your team better.


This comprehensive Qvidian vs Responsive comparison breaks down features, real G2 reviews, limitations, and pricing, then highlights the gaps both leave open.


## **TL;DR: Qvidian vs Responsive**


- Qvidian fits established enterprise teams that want tight governance, version control, and heavy reporting, and can take on a hands-on rollout.
- Responsive fits large organizations that need wide coverage: RFPs, security questionnaires, and a deep module and integration set, with the staff to climb its learning curve.
- Both are library-first. Their AI answers from content you maintain, so reviewers on each side say drafts need a careful pass before they are client-ready.
- If you want AI that writes from your live sources with citations and keeps your knowledge current on its own, an AI-native tool like[Inventive AI](https://www.inventive.ai/) (4.9 out of 5 on G2) belongs on your shortlist.

## **What is Qvidian? Enterprise RFP and proposal software**


Qvidian, now sold as Upland Qvidian since Upland bought it in 2017, is an enterprise RFP platform for[RFP](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/what-is-an-rfp-and-key-components-of-an-effective-rfp) ,[DDQ](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/ddq-meaning) , and proposal work. At its center sits a governed content library with version control, 70-plus reports, and a Microsoft Word add-in, and Upland bolted Qvidian AI Assist on in the last couple of years to generate and edit responses. It works best for large teams with a process to run, and reviewers most often knock its aging interface and the effort to set it up.


## **What is Responsive? RFP and security questionnaire software**


Responsive, formerly RFPIO, is response management software for RFPs,[security questionnaires](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/guide-saas-security-questionnaire) , DDQs, and other buyer requests. Teams store approved content in one central library, and Responsive’s AI drafts responses from that library. It also manages the work around each response: assigning questions to[subject-matter experts](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/sme-role) , routing drafts for review and approval, and tracking project progress.


Qvidian and Responsive both start with a content library your team maintains, then add AI over it. Inventive AI flips the order. It writes each answer from your approved knowledge, so responses stay grounded rather than hallucinated, and it spots conflicting or outdated content by itself to keep that knowledge current without manual cleanup. It holds a[4.9/5 on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/inventive-ai/reviews) across 80 reviews.

## **Qvidian vs Responsive: features, limitations, and reviews**


In this in-depth Responsive vs Qvidian evaluation, we look closely at what each platform does well, the top limitations cited in G2 reviews, pricing structures, and real user feedback. .


### **Qvidian**


#### **Key features**


- Governed library with version control, expiration dates, and scheduled review jobs
- Reporting depth: 70-plus prebuilt reports, a drag-and-drop builder, and dashboards
- Qvidian AI Assist for drafting, tone and length edits, and RFP analysis
- Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint add-ins, with Salesforce and Teams
- Role-based permissions and audit trails for enterprise sign-off


#### **Limitations (from G2 reviews)**


- The interface shows its age, and everyday tasks take more clicks than they should.
- Uploading content runs slow, and the library tends to open in a separate window.
- Search can miss the phrase you need, and the filters are thin.
- AI Assist is recent and, reviewers note, still finding its feet.
- Content upkeep is manual, with no automatic governance or live sync. See our[Qvidian alternatives guide](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/qvidian-competitors-alternatives) to compare modern tools that manage content hygiene automatically


#### **Pricing**


- Quote-only, licensed per named user
- A separate one-time implementation fee in the first year
- Annual, often multi-year terms (see our Qvidian pricing guide)


#### **What do reviewers say about Qvidian?**


[A Principal Bid Manager](https://www.g2.com/products/upland-qvidian/reviews/upland-qvidian-review-12222538) rates Qvidian 4.5/5. They value assigning tasks to the bid team in one place and reusing approved, high-scoring content from past RFPs. Their main complaint is limited AI. They want automatic response suggestions, quality scoring, and automated first drafts.

### **Responsive (formerly RFPIO)**


#### **Key features**


- One content library across RFPs, security questionnaires, and sales content
- A wide module set and one of the largest integration catalogs in the category
- AI drafting and a Q&A engine that sit on top of the library
- Project management and analytics built for large, multi-team bids
- Enterprise security, SSO, and access controls


#### **Limitations (from G2 reviews)**


- The learning curve is the single most common complaint; new users need time.
- The interface is busy, and it is not always clear who else is working or whether edits saved.
- Library search is not always accurate or easy to use.
- Some Excel formats break on upload, especially when matching answers to tables.
- AI drafts and translation still need review before responses go out. AI drafts and translation still need review before responses go out. Read our guide to the top[Responsive alternatives](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/rfpio-competitors-alternatives) if you want to avoid steep learning curves and manual library updates


#### **Pricing**


- Quote-based, priced per seat and module
- The entry Emerging edition starts near $10,000 a year
- Growth and Enterprise editions are quote-only and scale with modules and seats.


#### **Ratings**


[G2: 4.5 out of 5](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews) (1,313 reviews), the largest review base of the two.


#### **What do reviewers say about Responsive?**


A mid-market RFP Manager, Roberto G., rates Responsive[4.5/5](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews/responsive-formerly-rfpio-review-12461897) . They value the central library of approved content, which keeps responses consistent and saves time, and the ability to assign questions to SMEs across legal, security, and product. Their main complaint is that the library gets harder to manage as it grows. Finding the most relevant, up-to-date content takes extra time when several versions exist.

Fact to know before you choose


Qvidian and Responsive share the same two weak spots: content upkeep and draft quality. Stale and duplicate content builds up in the library, and AI drafts need a careful review before a buyer sees them. One outdated response in a live bid often goes unnoticed until after you submit.[Inventive AI](https://www.inventive.ai/) drafts from approved knowledge and flags outdated content automatically, so your content stays accurate with less manual effort.


## **Qvidian vs Responsive: the AI-native feature gap**


Neither Qvidian nor Responsive offers automated content governance or live sync with source systems. Both draft from a Q&A library your team updates by hand and work through RFPs one question at a time. Responsive adds a TRACE confidence score, and Qvidian shows no source or confidence score. AI drafts are only as reliable as the content behind them, and only[35%](https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/sales-ai-statistics-2024/) of sales professionals completely trust their organization’s data.


### **Where the AI gets its content**


Qvidian and Responsive draft from the library your team maintains, so a response is only as current as your last edit. An AI-native tool drafts from your connected sources directly, so it always uses current content without a separate library to update.


### **Catching outdated and conflicting content**


In both platforms, keeping content accurate is manual work: review cycles, expiration dates, and duplicate checks that people run. Neither flags conflicting or outdated responses automatically. An AI-native platform does, so stale content is caught before it reaches a buyer.


### **Showing where each response comes from**


AI drafts from both tools need careful review before they are client-ready. When each response shows its source and a confidence score, and flags anything the tool can’t back up, reviews go faster and carry less risk.


### **Finding the right content**


Search is a weak spot for both: Qvidian’s filters are thin, and Responsive’s library search is hit-or-miss. AI-native retrieval reads the full question in context, so it finds relevant content even when the wording doesn’t match a stored Q&A pair.


### **How fast your team can learn the tool**


Responsive’s steep learning curve is its most-cited complaint, and Qvidian’s interface feels dated. Complex tools slow the people using them: in a[Gartner](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2023-11-02-gartner-survey-finds-77-percent-of-sellers-struggle-to-complete-their-assigned-tasks-efficiently) survey of sellers’ experience with their technology, 77% said they struggle to complete their assigned tasks efficiently. A tool your whole team can learn quickly gets used more and delivers more value.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is Qvidian or Responsive better?


It depends on your team's workflow when you compare Qvidian and Responsive. Responsive offers broader module coverage and integrations (4.5/5 on G2 across 1,300+ reviews), while Qvidian provides tighter version governance and reporting depth (4.3/5 on G2). Both rely on manual library upkeep, so teams wanting faster, source-grounded drafting often test an AI-native alternative alongside them.


### Is Responsive the same as RFPIO?


Yes. RFPIO rebranded to Responsive. It is the same product and the same library-based architecture, now under the Responsive name.


### Which is harder to learn, Qvidian or Responsive?


Responsive. A steep learning curve is its most-cited complaint, driven by a broad, busy feature set. Qvidian is more focused, though reviewers still call its interface dated.


### How do Qvidian and Responsive price?


Qvidian is quote-only, per named user, with a separate implementation fee. Responsive is priced per seat and module, with its entry Emerging edition near $10,000 a year and higher editions quote-only.


### Do Qvidian and Responsive have AI?


Yes, both added AI drafting on top of their content library. In each, the AI answers from content your team maintains, and reviewers say output still needs a careful review before it is client-ready.


### What is the best AI-native alternative to Qvidian and Responsive?


Inventive AI is the AI-native option teams test against both most often. It writes from your connected sources with citations and confidence scores, governs content automatically, and holds a 4.9 out of 5 on G2.
